variants.name: can-biter
variants.grid: EXACTLY 10 frames laid out FIVE columns by TWO rows, equal square cells, read left-to-right top row then bottom. Canvas aspect 5:2, preferably 2560x1024. A smooth one-second idle/locomotion loop: tiny alternating pipe-pincer flex and rear cable-tail swish, can stays same scale and centered, green eye pulses subtly. Frames1 and10 near-identical for seamless loop.
variants.subject: A recognizable crushed ribbed TIN CAN mutated into a biting orbital bug. Oval dented mauve steel can forms shell, visible rolled circular rim and three broad ribs, torn lid at NORTH forms two sharp forward-facing metal mandibles. Two bright green eyes nestled in dark purple tissue just below north jaws. Pair of short crooked pipe pincers at sides, two short torn purple cable tails at SOUTH. The can silhouette and open biting lid must read instantly. Broad clear shapes, few high-contrast purposeful details.
variants.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Production game sprite sheet reskin for a top-down space shooter. Image 1 is the CURRENT enemy reference: preserve its upward-facing orientation, compact centered silhouette and scale, but replace spacecraft components with the specified recognizable mutated-trash creature. Image 2 is the established mutant-trash PALETTE reference: dusty mauve/lavender metal, dark violet organic mutation, dark purple outlines, restrained copper wear, luminous toxic-green eyes/seams. Original design, no brands or text. Crisp true low-resolution pixel art intended for 64x64 cells, deliberate chunky square pixel clusters, hard edges, limited coherent palette, no antialiasing, no smooth illustration, no gradient or bloom. Visually unmistakable concrete object plus creature, NOT abstract junk or shapeless blob. Orthographic TOP DOWN, front/jaws/eyes pointing UP toward top of image; no side-facing or portrait character. Keep creature centered at the same origin in every cell. Body including limbs occupies central 46% of each square cell, ample empty transparent padding. True transparent RGBA background, no painted checkerboard, scenery, floor, shadow, captions, labels, borders or cell grid.

variants.deathPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create the matching DESTRUCTION animation for the EXACT can-biter mutated-trash enemy in the supplied idle animation sheet. The supplied sheet is an identity/style reference, not a layout to preserve. Keep its unmistakable ribbed crushed tin-can shell, torn-lid jaws, two green eyes, pipe pincers and purple cable tails. Same dusty mauve metal, copper wear, purple mutation and toxic green. Crisp low-resolution 64x64-style game pixel art, strong purposeful square clusters, hard edges, limited palette. NO blurry illustration, bloom or antialiasing.
STRICT LAYOUT: FOUR columns by TWO rows of EQUAL SQUARE cells, 2:1 image aspect, preferably1536x768. No margins/gutters/grid/text/numbers. True transparent RGBA background, not painted checkerboard. All animation origins at cell centers. Read left to right top row then bottom. First frame is the exact intact creature, same identity and front pointing NORTH, occupying about40% of cell width and height. Use SAME scale and center for all frames, fragments stay inside each cell.
EIGHT-frame death: Frame1 exact intact creature. Frame2 brief green-white internal flash and visible casing cracks. Frame3 casing splits open, eye ruptures. Frame4 shell sections, claws/legs and wires burst outward. Frame5 separated recognizable curved ribbed can fragments and torn lid pieces plus short cables. Frame6 fragments shrink and sparks fade. Frame7 only a few very tiny dim scraps. Frame8 fully transparent.
No large smoke cloud obscuring identity, no fireball replacing the object, no scenery, no player, no rewards or glowing collectible orbs. Death is a sequence of the actual object's destruction, not a row of different creatures.

variants.name: battery-crawler
variants.grid: EXACTLY FIVE frames in ONE horizontal row of equal square cells. Canvas aspect5:1, preferably2560x512. A smooth repeating half-second idle/locomotion loop: short side legs flex in alternating pairs, green leakage subtly pulses, rigid battery casing stays identical and centered. Frame5 returns toward frame1.
variants.subject: A recognizable discarded rectangular BATTERY mutated into a crawling bug. Broad boxy mauve-purple casing with two clearly visible blunt terminals at NORTH, one casing corner cracked open revealing a single large luminous green eye and violet flesh. A simple dark split across the battery shell leaks a narrow toxic-green seam. Four short jointed scrap-metal legs, two on each side; two short frayed cable tails at SOUTH. No logos, letters, symbols or writing. Clearly battery-shaped, compact wide rectangular shell; not a spaceship or a generic beetle.

variants.subject: A recognizable broken square MONITOR mutated into an orbital parasite. Dusty mauve thick box frame encloses dark purple cracked glass, ONE large toxic-green angry eye grows through the screen facing toward NORTH; simple visible glass crack. Two broken metal mounting brackets form short forward-curving claws at LEFT and RIGHT, two torn cables trail SOUTH. Three-quarter top-down tilt just enough to show monitor frame thickness but no ground perspective. Clearly a cracked screen in a squared housing, NOT a vague face or futuristic spaceship. Keep the compact wide silhouette of the reference.

export.sampling: nearest neighbor; binary alpha threshold 128; one scale across each loop; row-origin registration
export.death_registration: First frame copied from corresponding exported idle; following frames use shared registration relative to generated intact cell; terminal frame transparent
